disclaimer: I'm a learning helper and can make mistakes. Don't share personal information.
privacyNote: Your questions stay on this device in FAQ mode.
starters: Do I need a PhD to work in quantum?
What is happening at the old South Works site?

noMatch.text: I don't have a good answer for that, and I don't want to guess. Try asking in a different way, or pick one of these questions. The Learn page is also a good place to start.
suggest: How can I learn quantum for free?

questions: What is quantum computing?
Explain quantum computers to me
What does quantum mean?
entries.answer: Your phone stores information as bits, tiny switches that are 0 or 1. A quantum computer uses qubits instead. Qubits follow the strange rules of quantum physics, which describe how very small things behave. They can help with a few hard problems, like studying molecules.

questions: What is quantum physics?
Do I need to know physics?
What are the rules of quantum physics?
entries.answer: Quantum physics is the set of rules that describe how very small things behave, like atoms and particles of light. You don't need a physics background to start here. The lessons use plain words and explain every new term the first time it shows up.

questions: What is a bit?
What is a bit in a regular computer?
How do computers store information?
entries.answer: A bit is the smallest piece of information in a regular computer. Think of it as a tiny switch that is either 0 or 1. Your phone and laptop store everything, from photos to games, as long lists of bits.

questions: What is a classical computer?
What is the difference between classical and quantum computers?
Are my phone and laptop classical computers?
entries.answer: A classical computer is an ordinary computer, like your laptop or phone. It stores information as regular bits that are 0 or 1. A quantum computer uses qubits, which can be in a blend of 0 and 1 until measured. Each kind is better at different jobs.

questions: What is a qubit?
What does qubit mean?
How is a qubit different from a bit?
entries.answer: A qubit is the quantum version of a bit. It can be a tiny object like an atom, a particle of light, or a very cold electric circuit. Until you measure it, it can be in a blend of 0 and 1. When you measure it, you always get a plain 0 or 1.

links.label: Try the qubit demo on the Home page

questions: What is superposition?
What does it mean for a qubit to be in a blend of 0 and 1?
Is a qubit both 0 and 1?
entries.answer: Superposition is the blend of 0 and 1 that a qubit can be in before you measure it. You never see the blend. You always get a plain 0 or 1, and the blend only sets the odds. A spinning coin is a loose comparison, but a qubit's blend is a real physical state.

questions: What happens when you measure a qubit?
What is measurement?
Why are quantum results random?
entries.answer: Measuring means checking a qubit's value. You always get a plain 0 or a plain 1, and the blend is gone. The blend only sets the odds, so a result can look random. That is why quantum programs run many times and tally the results.

links.label: Try the qubit demo on the Home page

questions: What is entanglement?
What does it mean for qubits to be entangled?
How do two qubits get linked?
entries.answer: Two qubits can be entangled. That means their measurement results are linked, even though each single result looks random on its own. Entanglement is one of the strange features that some quantum programs use. It is a real effect, not science fiction.

questions: What is a quantum gate?
What do gates do?
How do you change a qubit?
entries.answer: A quantum gate is a basic step that changes one or more qubits, like a single move in a game. Every gate can be undone by running its reverse. A quantum program is a list of gates followed by a measurement.

questions: What do the X and H gates do?
What is the Hadamard gate?
What is the NOT gate for qubits?
entries.answer: The X gate works like NOT: it swaps |0⟩ and |1⟩. The H gate (Hadamard) turns |0⟩ into an even blend, so measuring gives 0 or 1 about half the time each. Press them in the playground and see for yourself.

links.label: Open the playground in the Gates lesson

questions: What is phase?
What does the Z gate do?
What is the hidden plus or minus sign?
entries.answer: Phase is a hidden plus or minus sign on part of a qubit's state. Measuring can't see it right away, but it changes what later gates do. The Z gate flips it. Try Reset, H, Z, H in the playground and you land on |1⟩.

links.label: Try it in the Gates lesson

questions: What is a CNOT gate?
What are two-qubit gates?
How do gates connect qubits?
entries.answer: CNOT is a two-qubit gate. It uses one qubit to decide whether to flip another one. Two-qubit gates like it link qubits together, and they are how circuits make qubits work as a team.

questions: What is a quantum circuit?
How do you write a quantum program?
What is a circuit diagram?
entries.answer: A quantum circuit is a list of gates, in order, followed by a measurement. It is how people write a quantum program. You can build circuits on a simulator, even on your own laptop, before ever touching a real quantum computer.

questions: How does a quantum computer work?
How does a quantum computer run a program?
What is a shot?
keywords: how does a quantum computer work
entries.answer: A quantum program has three steps. First, prepare the qubits. Next, apply gates. Last, measure. Results are partly random, so the computer runs the program many times. Each run is called a shot, and the results get tallied, like counting votes.

questions: What are quantum computers made of?
Why are quantum computers so cold?
What kinds of qubits are there?
entries.answer: Qubits can be built in different ways. Some are tiny electric circuits chilled to near absolute zero. Others use trapped ions (charged atoms held in place), neutral atoms held by lasers, or particles of light. Each way has trade-offs, and all of them are fragile.

questions: Will quantum computers replace my laptop?
Will quantum computers replace regular computers?
Will I own a quantum computer someday?
entries.answer: No. Think of a quantum computer as a specialized power tool, like a tile saw. It is great for certain jobs and useless for most others. Regular computers will stay better for most things, and they will help control quantum machines too.

questions: Do quantum computers try every answer at once?
Is it true quantum computers are magic?
What are common myths about quantum computers?
entries.answer: That is a common myth. Quantum computers don't try every answer at once. They use the blend of 0 and 1 to steer toward good answers on certain problems. Quantum computers are not magic, and they help with specific problems only.

questions: Are quantum computers faster than regular computers?
What is quantum advantage?
Has a quantum computer beaten a regular computer?
entries.answer: Quantum advantage means doing a useful job faster or better than any regular computer. IBM and partners say they have shown early advantage on narrow problems, and other scientists are testing those claims. No one has shown broad advantage yet.

questions: What can quantum computers be used for?
Why do people care about quantum computing?
What problems can quantum computers solve?
entries.answer: Quantum computers may help simulate molecules and new materials, meaning model how they behave on a computer. IBM also lists energy and finance as areas to explore. They are specialized tools, so they will help with some problems and not others.

questions: What is a quantum algorithm?
What are quantum algorithms?
What is interference?
entries.answer: An algorithm is a step-by-step recipe for solving a problem. Quantum algorithms use interference, which is waves adding up or canceling out, to make wrong answers less likely and right answers more likely. They run on qubits, but they don't just try every answer.

questions: What is Grover's search?
How does a quantum computer search a list?
Can quantum computers search faster?
entries.answer: Grover's search finds one item in an unsorted list in about the square root of the usual number of steps. For 10,000 items, that is roughly 100 steps instead of thousands. It helps with specific problems, not everything.

questions: Can quantum computers break encryption?
What is Shor's algorithm?
What is post-quantum cryptography?
entries.answer: Shor's algorithm could split big numbers and break some public-key encryption, but only on a large, error-corrected quantum computer, and none exists today. Experts are already building new methods called post-quantum cryptography. In 2024, NIST published its first finished standards for it.

questions: What is quantum error correction?
How do you fix mistakes in a quantum computer?
What is a logical qubit?
entries.answer: Quantum error correction spreads the information of one qubit across many real qubits. Together they act as one steadier logical qubit. Helper qubits check for signs of errors without measuring the qubits that hold the data. It is costly, and today's machines are still working toward it.

questions: Why are qubits so fragile?
Why do quantum computers make mistakes?
What is decoherence?
entries.answer: Qubits are very delicate. Heat, vibration and stray signals can ruin a qubit's quantum state, and that loss is called decoherence. Quantum computers today are small and make many errors. Researchers are working on ways to keep qubits steady for longer.

questions: What is a quantum simulator?
How can I practice quantum programming without a quantum computer?
Can I run quantum programs on my laptop?
entries.answer: A quantum simulator is a program that runs on an ordinary computer and pretends to be a quantum computer. You build a circuit, run it, and see results. That lets you learn and fix mistakes without any quantum hardware.

questions: How many qubits can a simulator handle?
Can a laptop simulate a big quantum computer?
Why can't I simulate 100 qubits?
entries.answer: Each extra qubit roughly doubles the memory and time a simulator needs. IBM's documentation says most laptops can't simulate beyond about 32 qubits when noise is included. A general 100-qubit simulation is far out of reach, even for big supercomputers.

questions: What is quantum simulation?
Is a quantum simulator the same as quantum simulation?
Can quantum computers imitate nature?
entries.answer: Don't mix up two similar names. A quantum simulator is software on a regular computer. Quantum simulation means using a real quantum computer to imitate nature, such as molecules or materials. Researchers hope this could become one of the most useful uses of future quantum computers.

questions: What is a quantum compiler?
What is transpiling?
Why can't a real chip run my circuit as written?
entries.answer: A real quantum chip can only do a short list of built-in steps, and only some qubit pairs can work together. A compiler (often called a transpiler) translates your circuit so the chip can run it. It also trims wasted steps, because every extra step adds a chance of error.

questions: Do I need a PhD to work in quantum?
Can I get a quantum job without a degree?
What education do quantum jobs need?
entries.answer: Many quantum jobs do not usually need a PhD. Technicians, software developers, cybersecurity analysts and project managers all help build and run quantum computers. Some roles, like electricians, can start with a high school diploma plus an apprenticeship. Others call for a certificate or a degree. Check each posting.

questions: What jobs exist in quantum?
What careers are there in quantum computing?
What does a cryogenic plant technician do?
entries.answer: Quantum computers need people to build, run and protect them: technicians, software developers, cybersecurity analysts, and operations and project managers. Park planners in Chicago also list system operators, security staff, and cryogenic plant technicians, who run equipment kept at extreme cold.

questions: How much do quantum jobs pay?
Are there quantum jobs open right now?
Where can I apply for a quantum job?
entries.answer: I don't have verified pay numbers or job openings, so I won't guess. Pay and openings change often. Check the employer's own website and the Careers page, and ask a teacher or counselor to help you look for programs near you.

questions: Do I need to be good at math or coding?
What skills do I need for quantum?
Can I learn quantum if I am bad at math?
entries.answer: You can start with no physics background, and these lessons use plain words and short quizzes. For many software roles, strong coding, careful testing and curiosity matter most. Some programs, like Quantum Quickstart, suggest math such as trigonometry or pre-calculus.

questions: How can I learn quantum for free?
Where can I start learning quantum computing?
What free tools can I use to learn quantum?
entries.answer: Start with the lessons on this site, then try free tools. Quirk is a free, open-source simulator you drag and drop in your browser. IBM Quantum Learning is a library of courses that IBM says it offers free of charge. Qiskit and Cirq are open-source tools for coding.

questions: What is Quirk?
Is there a drag-and-drop quantum simulator?
How do I build a circuit by dragging gates?
entries.answer: Quirk is a drag-and-drop quantum circuit simulator that runs in your web browser. You drop gates onto a circuit and watch what happens. It is open source and made for exploring small circuits, so it is a great way to practice what you learn here.

questions: What is IBM Quantum Learning?
Does IBM have free quantum courses?
Where can I find courses from IBM?
entries.answer: IBM Quantum Learning is a library of courses for learning quantum computing with Qiskit. IBM says its learning resources are free of charge. Their courses go deeper than our short lessons, so they make a good next step. Check IBM's page for the current list.

questions: What are Qiskit and Cirq?
What software do people use to program quantum computers?
Is there open-source quantum software?
entries.answer: Qiskit and Cirq are free, open-source tools for writing and testing quantum programs. Open source means anyone can read the code and practice with it. Qiskit also has a transpiler you can try yourself, and both can run circuits on a simulator.

questions: What is the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park?
What is happening at the old South Works site?
Where is the quantum park in Chicago?
entries.answer: Illinois broke ground in September 2025 on the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park. It takes up about 128 acres at the south end of the old U.S. Steel South Works site on Chicago's far South Side. That is the first part of Quantum Shore, a larger 440-acre redevelopment. Steelmaking there ended in 1992. The state says it is investing $500 million in the park.

links.label: Read about it on the Home page

questions: What was South Works?
What happened to the steel mills in Chicago?
Why did the steel mills close?
entries.answer: South Works was a huge U.S. Steel mill on Chicago's South Side, and steelmaking there ended in 1992. For about a century, mills in South Chicago gave thousands of families steady work. When they closed, whole neighborhoods lost their paychecks. Each mill closed for different reasons, but the Southeast Chicago Historical Society says corporate restructuring, growing global competition and changing government policies were key.

links.label: See Chicago's tech revolutions on the Home page
The Closing of the Mills (SE Chicago Historical Society)

questions: Which companies are building at the quantum park?
What is PsiQuantum?
Is IBM coming to Chicago?
entries.answer: PsiQuantum is the anchor tenant, the first big company to commit to the park. It broke ground there on September 30, 2025, and says it uses light-based qubits. IBM's quantum computer is already running at UChicago's Hyde Park Labs on the South Side, switched on in November 2026. IBM says it will move to the park once the campus is complete.

links.label: Read the latest on the News page

questions: What is the Chicago Quantum Exchange?
Who works on quantum in Chicago?
Which universities do quantum research in Chicago?
entries.answer: The Chicago Quantum Exchange links universities, national labs and nearly 70 industry, international and nonprofit partners. It is based at the University of Chicago. Argonne National Laboratory and Fermilab are two of its anchor members. It works on research, training and economic growth in the Midwest.

questions: What do Argonne and Fermilab do for quantum?
What is Q-NEXT?
What is SQMS?
entries.answer: Two U.S. Department of Energy quantum research centers are in the Chicago area. Fermilab hosts one called SQMS, which works on keeping a qubit steady for longer. Argonne National Laboratory leads the other, called Q-NEXT. Both were renewed for five years.

questions: Is there a quantum network in Chicago?
What is the Chicago quantum network?
What is a quantum internet?
entries.answer: In 2022, the Chicago Quantum Exchange announced a quantum network with six nodes and 124 miles of fiber. It links Argonne in Lemont with two South Side buildings, one on the UChicago campus and one in Hyde Park. It was described as one of the nation's first public testbeds for quantum security.

questions: What is Quantum Quickstart?
Are there quantum summer programs for high school students?
Is there a free quantum camp in Chicago?
entries.answer: Quantum Quickstart is a one-week summer program run by the University of Chicago. It is for Illinois students in grades 9 to 11 who are at least 14. Selected students pay nothing, and Chicago students get preference. Dates and how to apply can change, so check the official page.

questions: Will the quantum park help my neighborhood?
Will South Side residents get jobs at the park?
How will the community benefit?
entries.answer: That is the goal, but it is not automatic. Park planners say they are talking with City Colleges of Chicago about training for all skill levels. Developer Related Midwest is helping fund a Quality of Life Plan for South Chicago. Neighbors deserve a real voice in the plan.

links.label: See the story on the Home page

questions: Why does this website exist?
What is Quantum South Side about?
What is this site for?
entries.answer: The land that powered the steel revolution is now home to the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park. This site helps students on Chicago's South and West Sides understand quantum technology and see the careers around it, so this time the benefits reach neighbors.

questions: How does this site work?
What can I do on this website?
Where should I start?
entries.answer: Learn has seven short lessons with quizzes. Careers shows quantum jobs, and many don't need a PhD. News and Research help you read about what's new. The Daily Puzzle gives you a new quantum puzzle every day. If you're not sure, start with Learn.

questions: How do the lessons work?
How many lessons are there?
Is there a quiz?
entries.answer: There are seven short lessons, from the basics to error correction and algorithms. Each has plain-language explanations, key terms and a quick quiz called Check yourself. The Gates lesson has a hands-on qubit playground. Mark a lesson complete to see your progress on the Home page.

questions: What is the Collapse Challenge?
What is the Daily Puzzle?
Is there a game on this site?
How does the daily puzzle work?
entries.answer: The Collapse Challenge is the daily puzzle. You get a Start state and a Target state, and you build gates to turn one into the other. A new puzzle comes every day, and your streak is saved on your device, or in your account if you are signed in. Practice mode lets you play any puzzle and never changes your streak.

questions: How do I get stars?
What does Peek do?
What is par?
entries.answer: In the Collapse Challenge, fewer gates earn more stars. Par is the fewest gates that can do the job, and matching it earns 3 stars. Peek measures the qubit once, so it collapses into a plain 0 or 1, and it costs one star. Practice mode never changes your streak.

questions: Where can I read quantum news?
Where can I find quantum research?
How do I keep up with quantum news?
entries.answer: The News page collects quantum stories, and the Research page shares new research. Both link to the original sources, so you can read the real thing. Always double-check important facts with the original article or paper.

questions: Do you collect my data?
Is this site safe for students?
Does this site track me?
entries.answer: As a guest, nothing leaves your device. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies. If this site offers accounts, an optional account stores only your email, a nickname and your progress. Please don't share personal information in this helper.

questions: Do I need an account?
Do I have to sign up or log in?
Can I use this site without an account?
entries.answer: No. Every feature works as a guest, and your progress stays on your device. If this site offers accounts, they are optional and let your progress follow you to other devices. You need to be 13 or older to make one. The Privacy page has the details.

questions: What does an account save?
What information does an account store?
Do you store my email or password?
entries.answer: If this site offers accounts, an account stores your email for logging in, a nickname you choose, and your progress and settings. It never collects your real name, birthdate, school, address, phone, race or location. Passwords are handled only by the sign-in service, never by us.

questions: Where is my progress saved?
How do I reset my progress?
Will I lose my progress?
entries.answer: As a guest, your progress is saved in your browser on this device, so it won't follow you to another phone or computer. If this site offers accounts, signing in saves it to your account instead. To erase it, open the Home page, find Your progress, and press Reset my progress.

questions: Is this site free?
Can teachers use this in class?
Can I use this site at school?
entries.answer: Yes, it is free. There is nothing to buy and no account is needed, so a whole class can use it without signing up. The lessons are short and have quizzes. The code is open source under the MIT License.

questions: Who made this website?
Who built this site?
What is the Black CS Success Summit Hackathon?
entries.answer: A team built this site for the Black CS Success Summit Hackathon 2026. The hackathon's theme was Past Revolutions, Future Power: Shaping Chicago's Quantum Future. It is a student-friendly project, so please double-check important facts with the sources we link.

questions: What can you help me with?
Are you a person or a robot?
Can you search the internet?
entries.answer: I'm a learning helper, not a person. In FAQ mode I match your question to a set of ready-made answers. I can't look things up online, I don't remember past chats, and I can make mistakes. When I'm not sure, I'll say so and point you to a page.

questions: Hello
Hi there
Hey, good morning
entries.answer: Hello! I'm happy you're here. Ask me about qubits, quantum careers, what is happening in Chicago, or how to use this site. You can also pick one of the starter questions.

questions: Thank you
Thanks a lot
That was helpful
entries.answer: You're welcome! Keep asking questions, because curiosity is how people get started in quantum. If you want to keep going, try a lesson on the Learn page.
